summary: The 401/invalid_token surge is real and its onset is firmly pinned to a clean step-change between the 14:00 and 14:02Z buckets (baseline ~0.2% → ~35-37%, sustained to 15:58Z), coinciding exactly with the only two changes in the entire fleet window: auth-service deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0, jjwt 0.11→0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten) at 14:00:00Z and the auth-service signing-key rotation cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 → k-2026-04) at 14:01:00Z. Infra saturation, latency, traffic surge, restarts and an api-gateway origin are all excluded, so the fault is one of those two auth-service changes. However, the evidence cannot separate them: the decisive discriminators (per-kid/per-error-code token-validation metric, per-instance/version/AZ breakdown, auth-service logs, any JWKS/secret-publication record) are all data-model absences confirmed by repeated queries, leaving H1 and H2 tied at low confidence and H3 (partial/canary rollout) neither confirmable nor excludable. Outcome is therefore inconclusive and the fix must be treated as an operational gamble (roll back the deploy and/or revert/stage the key rotation) rather than an evidence-supported conclusion.

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service v7.3.0 deploy (dep-5710) broke token parsing → 401s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 14:00:00Z deployment dep-5710 rewrote TokenValidator and migrated jjwt 0.11→0.12 (breaking parser API). The rewritten parser rejects a fraction of previously valid tokens (claim/clock-skew/algorithm handling), so validation returns invalid_token on roughly a third of calls. Origin is the released code; the fix would be to roll back dep-5710 or correct the parser (HIST-109 pattern). Kept active and moved to equal footing with H2 — nothing in the evidence separates the code artifact from the config value, and a breaking parser change would more naturally break a specific token class than all tokens, which is consistent with the observed ~1/3 plateau.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 deploys at 14:00:00Z with jjwt 0.11→0.12 breaking parser API and a rewritten TokenValidator; it is the only deployment in the 13:30-14:30Z onset window
The rewritten parser / new library defaults reject a fraction of tokens that previously validated (invalid_token)
auth-service error counter (counting 5xx; invalid_token surfaces there) jumps in a clean step at 14:00-14:02Z from ~0.2% to ~35-37%
api-gateway 401/error rate rises concurrently as a downstream carrier, with zero deployments of its own in the window
Users see 401 / forced logout on affected API calls

assumptions: A parser/library regression can reject ~1/3 rather than ~100% of tokens (only certain token shapes/claims hit the changed path) — asserted, not measured
The invalid_token/401 surfacing on the 5xx error counter is genuine, not a metric artifact
HIST-109 (a prior-incident lead, not evidence) describes the same mechanism

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2705 signing-key rotation (k-2025-10 → k-2026-04) at 14:01Z made a subset of tokens unverifiable
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The scheduled key rotation cfg-2705 at 14:01Z changed auth-service's jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04, so a cohort of tokens that carry (or require resolution of) the previous key id can no longer be verified and are returned as invalid_token. The fault ORIGINATES in the configuration value change, not in the released code; the fix would be to re-publish/accept the previous key id or stage the rotation (HIST-108 pattern). Kept active because the change is real, full-scope, and lands inside the onset minute — but its central mechanism is entirely unverified and the critic correctly flags it as a presumption.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 changes jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 → k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z, full scope on auth-service; it is the only config change in a widened 04-14 → 04-15 window
The signing key is handled inside auth-service config with no external JWKS/keystore/IdP node, so a key-id change directly alters in-process validation
A stable ~1/3 of tokens carry the old key id (or old-kid-derived state) and fail verification as invalid_token
auth-service error counter (5xx) steps from ~0.2% to ~35-37% in a single step at the 14:00→14:02Z boundary, coincident with the 14:01Z rotation
api-gateway rises concurrently as a downstream carrier with no deploy of its own
Users are logged out / hit 401 invalid_token on affected calls

assumptions: A key-id rotation can leave a stable ~1/3 of tokens unverifiable (old-kid cohort / not-yet-refreshed fraction) — never observed
No un-enumerated secret/JWKS publication job outside cfg-2705 also changed key state (gaps explicitly cannot rule this out)
HIST-108 (a prior-incident lead, not evidence) describes the same mechanism

ranked_hypotheses.title: Partial/canary or per-pod-inconsistent rollout of the auth-service change set
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Only a subset of auth-service replicas carry the new key id or library state (staggered rollout, propagation lag, or config not yet loaded everywhere), so requests routed to the stale/bad subset fail validation while the rest succeed — naturally producing a stable ~1/3 rate rather than 100%. Origin is the scoped/incomplete application of the auth-service change set (dep-5710 + cfg-2705); the fix is to complete the rollout or roll it back. Kept active at reduced confidence because the only natural explanation of the ~1/3 plateau is a subpopulation effect, yet the deployment and config schemas contain NO scope/canary/revision field, the metrics expose NO instance dimension, and no per-pod signal was ever measured — so the mechanism is structurally plausible but entirely unobserved.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 and cfg-2705 land at 14:00-14:01Z as distinct full-scope changes on auth-service
Only a fraction of auth-service replicas carry the new key id or library, creating inconsistent validation outcomes across the fleet
Requests hitting the stale/bad subset return invalid_token, yielding a partial ~1/3 (not 100%) failure rate
Measured error rate plateaus at a tight 35-37% — a stable minority of requests — with no bimodal signature in the only (aggregate) series

assumptions: A canary/staggered rollout or config-propagation lag actually occurred — F31/F32/F33/F36 return no scope field and report full service scope with no canary artifact
auth-service has multiple replicas across which a subset split could arise
The absence of a bimodal metric signature is an artifact of the missing instance dimension (F25), not evidence of uniformity

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared redis-cache neighbour fault induces token-validation 401s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service token validation touches the shared redis-cache (also consumed by portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service); a fault in that shared cache — possibly introduced with the 11:35Z market-data-service deploy dep-5699 — degrades validation state and causes invalid_token. Origin is the shared cache/dependency rather than the auth-service code or config.

causal_chain.claim: market-data-service dep-5699 deploys at 11:35Z into the shared redis-cache
The shared cache degrades auth-service token-validation state
auth-service returns invalid_token for affected calls

assumptions: Redis-cache is on the critical token-validation path (not stated in findings)
Something in the cache changed near 14:00Z to trigger the step — no such event is observed
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing rules it out: market-data-service dep-5699 landed at 11:35Z (F6), ~2.5 hours before the 14:00-14:02Z step-change (F1, F2), and the auth error rate was flat ~0.2% during that entire quiet interval. No change event occurred on redis-cache/user-db/kyc-provider in the window (F6, F7, F13, F14), and no per-component metric for them was ever obtained (gaps), so there is no positive evidence at all for a cache-side origin — only the structural fact that the cache is shared (F10).

facts.statement: auth-service error rate was flat at ~0.2-0.3% until 14:00:00Z, then jumped to 37.21% (max 38.34%) at 14:02:00Z and stayed at ~35-37% through 15:58Z — a step change, not a ramp.

The full fleet-wide deployment enumeration for 2026-04-15T00:00Z-15:59Z returned exactly two deployments: dep-5710 auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z (jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 breaking parser API; TokenValidator rewritten; status live, rolled_back_at null) and dep-5699 market-data-service v5.0.3 at 11:35:00Z; neither was rolled back.

The only config/flag/secret change in the window, including a widened query from 2026-04-14T00:00Z, is cfg-2705: auth-service 'jwt.signing.key_id' changed from 'k-2025-10' to 'k-2026-04' at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z by security-automation, described as a scheduled signing-key rotation.

api-gateway error rate jumped concurrently at the same onset (flat ~0.2-0.25% then 14.19% at 14:00Z and ~21% thereafter) but api-gateway had no deployment of its own in the window, so it is a downstream carrier rather than a cause.

auth-service infrastructure metrics are flat across onset: CPU ~37-40%, latency p99 ~88-92 ms, request rate ~390-408 req/s, restarts 0.0 for the whole 13:00-15:00Z window, excluding saturation, latency degradation, traffic surge and pod restarts.
auth-service's error_rate metric is defined as '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)', so the reported 36% counts the invalid_token/401 handling surfacing on the 5xx counter.

auth-service exposes exactly seven metric series (cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts) and none is a per-kid, per-error-code or per-failure-reason breakdown.

Both discriminator metric queries failed not_found (retryable=false): 'invalid_token' and 'token_validation_failures' are not available for auth-service, so no series can separate kid-cohort-specific (H2) from uniform parse/malformed (H1) rejection.

auth-service metrics expose no per-instance/pod, per-version/revision or per-AZ/node-pool dimension; 'error_rate_by_instance' returned not_found and all available metrics are service-level aggregates.

The aggregate error_rate shows a single clean step from a pre-onset plateau (~0.18-0.24% avg) to a post-onset plateau (~35-37% avg) with no intermediate second population, but being unlabelled it cannot localise which tokens fail.

auth-service logs are unsearchable for the whole investigation window: query_logs returned 'backend unavailable (503)' after 3 retries for both ERROR-level and general queries, consistent with the reported identity-namespace log-pipeline outage.

The deployment record schema for dep-5710 contains no rollout-scope fields (no canary %, AZ, node pool or revision label) and the config-change schema has no scope field either; dep-5710 is returned identically under all-services and auth-service-scoped queries, so a partial/staged rollout cannot be represented or observed.

No record type exists for JWKS publication, k8s secret update, or cert/secret rotation: the config-change query for the entire 2026-04-14 day returned count 0 and the auth-service dependency graph contains no key-store/JWKS/IdP node (nodes are api-gateway, auth-service, user-db, redis-cache, kyc-provider).
redis-cache is a shared cache consumed by auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service, and market-data-service (deployed 11:35Z) is a neighbour on that shared cache.

Two historical precedents match the exact symptom pair ('401 invalid_token', 'users logged out'): HIST-108 (config_change, key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded JWKS) and HIST-109 (bad_deployment, JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default). They are leads and do not select between the deploy and the rotation.

assumptions: It is assumed the ~36% error rate reflects genuine invalid_token/401 rejections and not a metric artifact (the error_rate is defined as HTTP 5xx %; corroborated by the reported symptom but never observed in logs).

It is assumed the fault originates in one of the two enumerated auth-service changes; this rests on the assumption that no un-modeled change (k8s secret update, JWKS publication job, feature-flag toggle outside the config store) occurred — explicitly unverifiable in this data model.
It is assumed a parser/library regression could reject ~1/3 rather than ~100% of tokens (only certain token shapes/claims hit the changed path); this was asserted, not measured.
It is assumed a key-id rotation could leave a stable ~1/3 of tokens unverifiable (old-kid cohort / not-yet-refreshed fraction); this mechanism was never observed.
It is assumed that the absence of a bimodal metric signature reflects the missing per-instance dimension rather than genuine uniformity, so H3 (partial/canary rollout) remains formally possible.
It is assumed auth-service runs multiple replicas such that a subset split could in principle arise, though the tooling exposes no instance count.
It is assumed the referenced prior incidents (HIST-108/HIST-109) describe mechanisms comparable to the current changes; they are historical leads, not evidence.

timeline.event: Start of the fleet-wide change-enumeration window; config-change query for the full 2026-04-14 day returned count 0, i.e. no earlier config/secret change was recorded.
market-data-service v5.0.3 (dep-5699) deployed; a neighbour on the shared redis-cache, but followed by ~2.5 hours of flat auth error rate, so timing rules it out as the trigger.
api-gateway error rate still flat at ~0.2-0.25% and auth-service error rate still at baseline ~0.2% — pre-onset steady state.
Last clean pre-onset bucket: auth-service error_rate avg 0.23%, max 0.31%.

auth-service v7.3.0 (dep-5710) deployed by d.verma — 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation', jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API), TokenValidator rewritten; status live, rolled_back_at null. The 14:00Z coarse bucket later averages 18.71% with max 38.34%, showing onset inside that bucket.
api-gateway error rate jumps concurrently (14.19%, max 21.73%) and stays ~21% thereafter, marking the gateway as a downstream carrier of the auth 401s.
cfg-2705 applied: auth-service 'jwt.signing.key_id' changed k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 by security-automation ('Scheduled signing-key rotation') — full-scope scalar change, one minute after the deploy.
auth-service error_rate reaches 37.21% (max 38.34%) and holds a tight 35-37% plateau for the remainder of the window; no intermediate second population is seen.
INC-007 reported by on-call SRE: about a third of token validations fail with 401; identity-namespace log pipeline down since the morning so auth-service logs are not searchable.

Investigation window closes with the plateau unbroken (last avg 36.91%), both auth changes still live (no rollback), and all decomposing signals unavailable: no per-kid/-error-code metric, no per-instance/-version breakdown, no logs, no JWKS/secret record type.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation with the best-evidenced single lever: roll back auth-service deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0) to the previous revision, then watch auth-service error_rate at 2-minute resolution for return to ~0.2%. If it does not drop within one or two buckets, immediately revert cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id back to k-2025-10).
recommended_actions.rationale: Both candidate origins are full-scope changes inside the 14:00-14:01Z onset cluster, and no telemetry separates them; a single-revert test is the only remaining discriminator. Rolling back the deploy first is preferred because it is the reversible code artifact with the breaking-library note and a matching precedent (HIST-109), and it is a safe action independent of which hypothesis holds.

recommended_actions.action: If the deploy rollback leaves the rate elevated, revert or re-stage the cfg-2705 key rotation: re-publish/accept the previous key id (k-2025-10) or stage the rotation so all consumers load it before cutover, and confirm error_rate step-down.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is tied at the same confidence and names a different origin and fix; the key-id rotation at 14:01Z is the other full-scope change inside onset, with a matching precedent (HIST-108, 're-published previous key; staged rotation'). This is the second half of the same single-lever discrimination experiment.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument before the next rotation: add a token-validation failure metric with kid and error-reason labels (e.g. invalid_token{failure_reason=expired|bad_kid|malformed, kid=...}) so the H1-vs-H2 discriminator exists in telemetry.
recommended_actions.rationale: The decisive discriminator is absent by design: available_metrics has no per-kid or per-error-code series and both 'invalid_token' and 'token_validation_failures' returned not_found, making the parse-wide vs kid-cohort distinction unanswerable.

recommended_actions.action: Add an instance/version/revision dimension to auth-service metrics (or a per-pod error_rate) so a subset-vs-uniform failure can be measured, and confirm replica count.
recommended_actions.rationale: No per-instance/per-version/AZ dimension exists ('error_rate_by_instance' returned not_found) and every metric is a service-level aggregate, so H3 (partial/canary rollout) can be neither confirmed nor excluded and the ~1/3 plateau cannot be decomposed.

recommended_actions.action: Restore or bypass the identity-namespace log pipeline and re-query auth-service ERROR logs for the 14:00-14:02Z boundary to recover the invalid_token error text and any per-kid detail.
recommended_actions.rationale: auth-service logs were unsearchable for the entire window (503 after retries), so the invalid_token signature is inferred from the report only; log text is the cheapest surviving substitute for the missing metric discriminator.

recommended_actions.action: Model key/JWKS publication events (secret update, key-publication job status, per-pod key-id version) in the change store and dependency graph, and add a scope/canary/revision field to deployment and config-change records.
recommended_actions.rationale: There is no record type for JWKS/secret rotation and no scope field on deployments or config changes, so the HIST-108 mechanism ('new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS') is untestable and staged rollouts are unobservable even if they occur — the root cause of this investigation's inability to converge.

recommended_actions.action: Adopt staged key rotations and deploy/rotation decoupling: never land a signing-key rotation within minutes of an auth-service code deploy, and gate rotations on confirmed propagation to all replicas.
recommended_actions.rationale: Both prior incidents in this service (key rotation published before pods loaded JWKS; library upgrade changing clock-skew default) share this symptom set, and the 14:00/14:01Z contiguity is exactly what made the current incident impossible to attribute.

data_gaps: No per-kid, per-error-code or per-failure-reason token-validation metric exists for auth-service (invalid_token and token_validation_failures both not_found); available metrics are limited to cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts. Limits the conclusion to 'one of the two auth-service changes' without saying which.

No per-instance/pod, per-version/revision or per-AZ/node-pool breakdown exists (error_rate_by_instance not_found); every metric is a service-level aggregate, so the ~1/3 plateau cannot be decomposed and H3 cannot be confirmed or excluded.

auth-service logs are unsearchable (503 backend unavailable across the window; identity-namespace log-pipeline outage), so the invalid_token signature itself was never observed and no onset-to-the-minute or per-pod evidence could be recovered.

No record type exists for JWKS publication, k8s secret updates, cert/secret rotation, or per-pod key-id/stale-config state (the 2026-04-14 config query returned count 0 and there is no key-store/JWKS node in the dependency graph), so an un-enumerated key/secret event outside cfg-2705 cannot be ruled out.

Deployment and config-change schemas contain no canary %, AZ, node-pool or revision field, and dep-5710 is returned identically under all scopes; whether the rollout was staged is unknowable from this data.

Blast radius beyond api-gateway is unconfirmed: queries for other identity-namespace/dependent services returned budget_exhausted, and no infra anomaly queries (memory, connection saturation, DNS, neighbour restarts) for the identity namespace were run.
No per-component metric for redis-cache, user-db or kyc-provider was obtained, so a shared-cache/user-db co-factor cannot be fully excluded even though no change event accompanied one.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A rollback of dep-5710 alone causing error_rate to return to ~0.2% within one or two buckets would move the conclusion to H1 (parser/library regression) as root cause; conversely, an isolated revert of cfg-2705 restoring baseline would move it to H2 (key rotation).

A per-kid token-validation metric or log recovery showing failures concentrated in an old/expired kid cohort would confirm H2; showing failures spread uniformly across kids and dominated by malformed/parse errors would confirm H1.

A per-instance/per-version breakdown showing some replicas at ~0.2% while others at ~100% (averaging to ~36%) would confirm H3 (partial/canary or stale-config rollout) and mean the fix is completing or rolling back the rollout, not the change semantics.
Discovery of an un-modeled change event (a JWKS publication job, k8s secret update, or feature-flag toggle) near 14:00-14:02Z would introduce a new origin and could demote both current leaders.
Evidence that redis-cache, user-db or kyc-provider degraded near 14:00Z (previously unobtained per-component metrics) would reopen the shared-dependency hypothesis that timing currently rejects.

findings.statement: auth-service error rate was flat at ~0.2-0.3% until 14:00:00Z (avg 0.21%, max 0.26%), then jumped to 37.21% (max 38.34%) at 14:02:00Z and remained elevated ~35-37% for the rest of the window (to 15:58:00Z). The transition happened between the 14:00 and 14:02 two-minute buckets — a step-change, not a gradual ramp.

The earlier 4-minute-cadence query shows the same transition smeared across the 14:00Z bucket: prior buckets all ~0.16-0.27%, the 14:00:00Z bucket averages 18.71% with max 38.34%, i.e. the onset falls inside that bucket (after 14:00, by 14:04 avg is 37.12%). This confirms onset near 14:00-14:02Z and shows why a coarse bucket makes onset look earlier than the true step.

api-gateway error rate shows a concurrent correlated jump at the same onset: flat ~0.2-0.25% through 13:54Z, then 14.19% (max 21.73%) at 14:00:00Z and ~21% thereafter — i.e. the gateway is a downstream carrier of the auth 401s, not a healthy control.

auth-service infrastructure metrics are flat across the onset — CPU ~37-40% (no spike), latency p99 stable ~88-92 ms, request rate stable ~390-408 req/s, and restarts stay 0.0 for the entire 13:00-15:00Z window. The 401 surge is therefore not caused by resource saturation, latency degradation, traffic surge or pod restarts of auth-service.

auth-service exposes these metrics: cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts. Note the unit of error_rate is '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)' — so the 36% error rate is counted as 5xx responses at the service, i.e. the invalid_token/401 handling surfaces on the 5xx counter.

Full-window deployment enumeration across ALL services for 2026-04-15T00:00Z–15:59Z returned exactly 2 deployments: dep-5710 auth-service v7.3.0 at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z by d.verma ('Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation', changes: 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten'), status 'live', rolled_back_at null; and dep-5699 market-data-service v5.0.3 at 11:35:00Z (''Fix symbol mapping', 'update ISIN map'), status 'live', not rolled back. Neither was rolled back as of 15:59Z.

The only config/flag/secret change in the window (confirmed against a widened 2026-04-14T00:00Z start) is cfg-2705: auth-service key 'jwt.signing.key_id' changed from 'k-2025-10' to 'k-2026-04' at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z by security-automation, described as 'Scheduled signing-key rotation'. This is a key rotation at full scope on the reported service, one minute after the auth-service deploy.

The two auth-service changes are contiguous in time: deploy at 14:00:00Z and signing-key rotation at 14:01:00Z, i.e. ~11-12 minutes before the 14:12Z incident report. Order matters here: the library upgrade landed first, the key id rotation one minute later.

auth-service's dependency map is small: edges auth-service->user-db (db), auth-service->redis-cache (cache), auth-service->kyc-provider (external), and api-gateway->auth-service (http). Notably there is NO separate token store, key store, JWKS endpoint or IdP node in the graph — so token validation paths through user-db, the shared redis-cache, and the external kyc-provider, with the signing key handled inside auth-service config rather than an external key service.

redis-cache is the shared component with the widest blast radius: 'shared': true and consumed by auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service (all kind 'cache'). A neighbouring service that writes into this shared cache can therefore affect auth-service token validation indirectly; market-data-service — which deployed at 11:35Z and depends on redis-cache — is one such neighbour.

Two historical precedents match this incident's exact symptom set ('401 invalid_token', 'users logged out'): HIST-108 (2025-10-01, '401s after JWT signing key rotation', services auth-service, root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', category config_change, resolution 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation', match_score 5) and HIST-109 (2025-07-11, 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default', category bad_deployment, resolution 'Rolled back; pinned skew config', match_score 4). These are leads, not evidence: HIST-108's published-key-before-JWKS-load mechanism and HIST-109's skew-default mechanism are distinct causes of identical symptoms.

Both attempted discriminator metrics returned not_found (retryable=false): querying 'invalid_token' and 'token_validation_failures' on auth-service both fail, each returning the same 7-metric list as the only data available. So neither an 'invalid_token split by kid' series nor an 'old-key/expired-key vs malformed/parse-error' rejection counter exists for auth-service in this telemetry.

The one remaining auth-service series that could plausibly have carried a failure-reason dimension, rate_limited_per_min, is a single unlabelled scalar series (unit 'req/min') that stays flat across the onset: ~2.0/min through 13:30–14:00Z and ~1.79–2.47/min for the rest of the window (min 0.96, max 3.23, mean 2.01 over 150 points). It shows no step at 14:00–14:02Z and carries no error-code/kid breakdown.

The sub-metric for 'old-key/expired-key vs malformed/parse-error' rejection does not exist, so H2 (kid-cohort-specific failure) cannot be distinguished from H1 (uniform parse/malformed failure) from any auth-service token-validation metric. The discriminator series required by T5 is absent from the telemetry.

The aggregate error_rate over 13:30–15:59Z confirms a single clean step at the 14:00→14:02Z boundary (flat ~0.18–0.24% avg through the 13:58 bucket, then 37.15% avg at 14:02:00Z, sustained ~34.6–37.3% thereafter; min 0.13, max 40.33, mean 28.5). This is consistent with a full-scope step change and shows no partial/secondary step that would suggest a canary subpopulation, but it cannot localise WHICH tokens fail because it is unlabelled.

auth-service logs remain unsearchable during 13:30–15:59Z: two query_logs attempts both returned backend unavailable (503) after 3 retries. This is consistent with the reported identity-namespace log-pipeline outage and means no log-derived per-kid/per-error-code split can be recovered either.

auth-service metric API exposes NO per-instance/pod, per-version/revision, or per-AZ/node-pool dimension. An explicit breakdown query for 'error_rate_by_instance' returned not_found: "service 'auth-service' has no metric 'error_rate_by_instance'", and the full available_metrics list is exactly [cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts] -- all service-level aggregates. Per-instance/per-version breakdown is therefore UNAVAILABLE.

Because only a single aggregate error_rate series exists (one value per bucket), the 36% is a service-wide average, not one of several per-pod values. There is no data showing a bimodal split of instances at ~0.2% vs ~36%; the series itself shows a clean step from a pre-onset plateau (~0.18-0.24%) to a post-onset plateau (~35-37%) with no intermediate second population.

The 13:30-15:59Z error_rate window shows the onset step between the 13:58:00Z bucket (avg 0.23, max 0.31) and the 14:02:00Z bucket (avg 37.15, max 38.34); there is a data gap at 14:00:00Z (bucket_seconds=240, no point emitted for 14:00). After onset the elevated plateau is tight: 35.13-37.27% avg across every subsequent bucket to 15:58Z (last avg 36.91), i.e. it does not return toward baseline at any point in the window.

Supporting infra aggregates remain flat across the same window, so they carry no per-instance signal either: request_rate stays ~394-410 req/s (min 366.46, max 435.3, mean 401.3, no step at 14:00) and cpu_pct stays ~37-39% (min 34.24, max 42.31, mean 38.1). Neither shows a subset-sized discontinuity that would reveal a partial rollout.

auth-service error logs are unretrievable (consistent with the reported identity-namespace log-pipeline outage): query_logs for ERROR-level entries 13:30-15:59Z failed with "backend unavailable (503) (gave up after 3 attempts)". No log-side confirmation of per-pod behaviour is possible.

The 36% level is best read as an all-replica aggregate: with only one series and a tight 35-37% plateau, the metric is consistent with the fault affecting every instance uniformly, but the metric cannot distinguish 'all replicas at 36%' from 'some replicas at ~100% averaging to 36%'. The absence of a bimodal signature is not proof of uniformity because the tool exposes no instance split -- this must be inferred from a non-metric source (deployment scope / config scope), both of which F12/F13/F6 already report at full service scope with no canary/subset field.

The full deployment record for dep-5710 contains no rollout-scope fields at all: it is exactly {id, service, version, deployed_at, author, summary, changes[], status, rolled_back_at} with values dep-5710 / auth-service / v7.3.0 / 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z / d.verma / 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten' / status 'live' / rolled_back_at null. There is no canary percentage, no AZ, no node pool, and no revision label, so the schema cannot represent a partial/staged rollout.

The same dep-5710 record is returned identically regardless of scope filter: querying all services for 13:00-15:59Z (tc-029) and auth-service specifically (tc-027) both yield count 1 with the identical field set — no field distinguishes a subset of instances. No additional rollout record (canary step, second revision, staged wave) exists in 2026-04-15T13:00Z-15:59Z.

Config-change records carry no scope field either: the schema is {id, service, key, old_value, new_value, changed_at, author, description}. The only change in 2026-04-14T00:00Z-15:59Z is cfg-2705 (auth-service, jwt.signing.key_id: k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04, 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z, security-automation, 'Scheduled signing-key rotation'), and it is a single scalar key value — it cannot encode a per-instance/partial rotation.

There is no modeled record type for a JWKS/key-publication event, k8s secret update, or cert/secret rotation outside the config-change store: (a) the two known tool schemas (get_deployments, get_config_changes) expose no secret/JWKS/cert field or service; (b) querying config changes for the ENTIRE 2026-04-14 day returns count 0, confirming no such event is filed as a config change that day; (c) the auth-service dependency graph contains no key-store/JWKS/IdP node (nodes are api-gateway, auth-service, user-db, redis-cache, kyc-provider only). So any JWKS-publish or k8s-secret-update step is NOT observable in this data model.

The HIST-108 mechanism ('published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', config_change, match_score 3.5 in this query) cannot be tested with available records: there is no JWKS-load, secret-propagation or per-pod key-id telemetry field anywhere in the deployment, config-change, or dependency outputs. HIST-108 and HIST-109 ('JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default') both match the symptom pair '401 invalid_token' and remain distinguishable only by their category (config_change vs bad_deployment), not by any observed rollout-scope evidence.
